resources.string: Let your day follow phone activity, at any time of day. Compare it with your previous day end.
Requires Android 9 or newer for screen and lock events.

After enough time awake, five minutes with the phone locked or screen off marks a possible day end. A longer rest confirms that same time. Sustained phone use starts the next day; short checks during a confirmed rest do not. This estimates time away from your phone, not sleep. No bedtime or wake-up time is required. Percentage checkpoints pause in this mode because the final day length is unknown. Clock checkpoints keep their schedules.
Rest needed to confirm an end
%1$s without phone use. Shorter breaks do not finish the day. Changing this starts a fresh observation while keeping history.
Time awake before a rest can end the day
%1$s from the day start to putting the phone down. Helps ignore naps and low-phone periods soon after waking.
Optional. A rest that overlaps these hours cannot end the day. Choose any range, including one across midnight.
Choose a time before enabling awake hours
Choose different beginning and end times for the hours you want to exclude.
Confirmed ends will appear here, with earlier or later comparisons.

Times are estimates from this phone, shown in your current time zone. Comparisons use the shortest difference on the local clock, up to 12 hours in either direction. Earlier and later describe timing, without a target schedule.
Same clock time as previous end
Use this if you were awake during a long break from your phone.
Ignore the possible end at %1$s and continue this day.
Ignore the estimated end at %1$s if you were awake during that break.
Usage Access granted. Automatic starts and phone-free rest detection are available.
Usage Access is needed to follow phone-free rest. Tap to open Android settings.
Phone use needed to start a day
%1$d minutes of uninterrupted unlocked phone use. Shorter checks after a confirmed rest do not start the next day.
The previous end is a comparison reference. Passing it does not complete this day.
